distinguishing_features: Compliant elastomer coating (low-modulus polyurethane/nylon-PU laminate) on the pipe bottom
Mechanism of reducing peak contact stress by increasing impact duration and hysteresis damping
Thickness 15-30 mm with modulus ~15 MPa, installed by internal access
No new instrumentation; uses existing pressure and visual inspection
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce abrasive wear of a hydro-transport pipeline bottom caused by sliding bed load without relying on increased hardness or frequent inspection?
parsed.viable_reason: Sliding bed load erosion is abrasive sliding wear, not impact-dominated; a compliant elastomer layer does not reduce the total normal force or cutting/plowing wear and is itself susceptible to abrasion, so the stated mechanism is not physically sound for the stated failure mode.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Because the mechanism is not viable for sliding bed load, it cannot be a non-obvious improvement; moreover, compliant linings are a known alternative to hard-facing for slurry abrasion, so the design change would be routine.
